title: A Token Is Not a Unit of Difficulty: Segmentation Controls Where Adaptive Computation Goes Inside a Word
abstract: arXiv:2611.00983v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Early-exit language models decide for each token how much computation to spend, usually by stopping once the prediction is confident. Yet a token is not a fixed unit: tokenizers cut words into different numbers of pieces in different languages. We ask where inside a word such a policy spends its budget. In Qwen3, along two adaptive axes (the timesteps of a spiking conversion and the layers of the original Transformer), confidence stopping gives the continuation pieces of a word less computation than its first piece in English, German, and Turkish, but more in Bangla. Segmentation drives this. Re-segmenting the same parallel passages with BPE-dropout shifts the gap by up to eight exits on both axes, small models trained under two tokenizers shift Bangla's gap by six exits, and BLOOM and mGPT, which split Bangla less finely, give it the English pattern. Characters per token do not predict the gap across languages; within-word surprisal exp

translated_title: 词元不是难度单位：分词方式控制着自适应计算在词内部的去向
translated_abstract: 提前退出语言模型为每个词元决定花费多少计算量，通常在预测足够置信时即停止。然而词元并不是一个固定单位：分词器在不同语言中会把单词切分成不同数量的片段。我们探究这类策略在词内部把计算预算花在了哪里。在Qwen3中，沿着两个自适应轴（脉冲化转换的时间步和原始Transformer的层），置信停止策略在英语、德语和土耳其语中给词的后续片段分配的计算量少于其首个片段，但在孟加拉语中却相反。分词方式是这一现象的驱动因素：用BPE-dropout对相同的平行语料重新分词，会使两个轴上的差距最多偏移八次退出；在两种分词器下训练的小模型使孟加拉语的差距偏移六次退出；而对孟加拉语切分不那么细的BLOOM和mGPT则呈现出英语的模式。每词元字符数无法预测跨语言的差距；词内惊奇度exp（原文此处截断）
tldr: 该论文发现提前退出语言模型中词内计算量的分配由分词方式而非语言本身决定——英语、德语和土耳其语中词的后续片段获得比首个片段更少的计算，而孟加拉语相反，且重新分词或更换分词器即可偏移甚至逆转这一差距。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that segmentation, not the language itself, determines how early-exit adaptive computation is distributed inside a word: continuation pieces receive less computation than the first piece in English, German, and Turkish but more in Bangla, and re-segmenting with different tokenizers shifts or reverses this gap.
